451:     for level, intervals in enumerate(intervals_hier[1:], 1):
452:         # Make sure this level is consistent with the root
453:         label_current = util.generate_labels(intervals)
454:         validate_structure(intervals_hier[0], label_top, intervals, label_current)
455: 
456:         # Make sure all previous boundaries are accounted for
457:         new_bounds = set(util.intervals_to_boundaries(intervals))
458: 
459:         if boundaries - new_bounds:
460:             warnings.warn(
461:                 "Segment hierarchy is inconsistent " "at level {:d}".format(level)
462:             )
463:         boundaries |= new_bounds
464: 
465: 
466: def tmeasure(
467:     reference_intervals_hier,
468:     estimated_intervals_hier,
469:     transitive=False,
470:     window=15.0,
471:     frame_size=0.1,
472:     beta=1.0,
473: ):
474:     """Compute the tree measures for hierarchical segment annotations.
475: 
476:     Parameters
477:     ----------
478:     reference_intervals_hier : list of ndarray
479:         ``reference_intervals_hier[i]`` contains the segment intervals
480:         (in seconds) for the ``i`` th layer of the annotations.  Layers are
481:         ordered from top to bottom, so that the last list of intervals should
482:         be the most specific.
483:     estimated_intervals_hier : list of ndarray
484:         Like ``reference_intervals_hier`` but for the estimated annotation
485:     transitive : bool
486:         whether to compute the t-measures using transitivity or not.
487:     window : float > 0
488:         size of the window (in seconds).  For each query frame q,
489:         result frames are only counted within q +- window.
490:     frame_size : float > 0
491:         length (in seconds) of frames.  The frame size cannot be longer than
492:         the window.
493:     beta : float > 0
494:         beta parameter for the F-measure.
495: 
496:     Returns
497:     -------
498:     t_precision : number [0, 1]
499:         T-measure Precision
500:     t_recall : number [0, 1]
501:         T-measure Recall
502:     t_measure : number [0, 1]
503:         F-beta measure for ``(t_precision, t_recall)``
504: 
505:     Raises
506:     ------
507:     ValueError
508:         If either of the input hierarchies are inconsistent
509: 
510:         If the input hierarchies have different time durations
511: 
512:         If ``frame_size > window`` or ``frame_size <= 0``
513:     """
514:     # Compute the number of frames in the window
515:     if frame_size <= 0:
516:         raise ValueError(
517:             "frame_size ({:.2f}) must be a positive " "number.".format(frame_size)
518:         )
519: 
520:     if window is None:
521:         window_frames = None
522:     else:
523:         if frame_size > window:
524:             raise ValueError(
525:                 "frame_size ({:.2f}) cannot exceed "
526:                 "window ({:.2f})".format(frame_size, window)
527:             )
528: 
529:         window_frames = int(_round(window, frame_size) / frame_size)
530: 
531:     # Validate the hierarchical segmentations
532:     validate_hier_intervals(reference_intervals_hier)
533:     validate_hier_intervals(estimated_intervals_hier)
534: 
535:     # Build the least common ancestor matrices
536:     ref_lca = _lca(reference_intervals_hier, frame_size)
537:     est_lca = _lca(estimated_intervals_hier, frame_size)
538: 
539:     # Compute precision and recall
540:     t_recall = _gauc(ref_lca, est_lca, transitive, window_frames)
541:     t_precision = _gauc(est_lca, ref_lca, transitive, window_frames)
542: 
543:     t_measure = util.f_measure(t_precision, t_recall, beta=beta)
544: 
545:     return t_precision, t_recall, t_measure
546: 
547: 
548: def lmeasure(
549:     reference_intervals_hier,
550:     reference_labels_hier,
551:     estimated_intervals_hier,
552:     estimated_labels_hier,
553:     frame_size=0.1,
554:     beta=1.0,
555: ):
556:     """Compute the tree measures for hierarchical segment annotations.
557: 
558:     Parameters
559:     ----------
560:     reference_intervals_hier : list of ndarray
561:         ``reference_intervals_hier[i]`` contains the segment intervals
562:         (in seconds) for the ``i`` th layer of the annotations.  Layers are
563:         ordered from top to bottom, so that the last list of intervals should
564:         be the most specific.
565:     reference_labels_hier : list of list of str
566:         ``reference_labels_hier[i]`` contains the segment labels for the
567:         ``i`` th layer of the annotations
568:     estimated_intervals_hier : list of ndarray
569:     estimated_labels_hier : list of ndarray
570:         Like ``reference_intervals_hier`` and ``reference_labels_hier``
571:         but for the estimated annotation
572:     frame_size : float > 0
573:         length (in seconds) of frames.  The frame size cannot be longer than
574:         the window.
575:     beta : float > 0
576:         beta parameter for the F-measure.
577: 
578:     Returns
579:     -------
580:     l_precision : number [0, 1]
581:         L-measure Precision
582:     l_recall : number [0, 1]
583:         L-measure Recall
584:     l_measure : number [0, 1]
585:         F-beta measure for ``(l_precision, l_recall)``
586: 
587:     Raises
588:     ------
589:     ValueError
590:         If either of the input hierarchies are inconsistent
591: 
592:         If the input hierarchies have different time durations
593: 
594:         If ``frame_size > window`` or ``frame_size <= 0``
595:     """
596:     # Compute the number of frames in the window
597:     if frame_size <= 0:
598:         raise ValueError(
599:             "frame_size ({:.2f}) must be a positive " "number.".format(frame_size)
600:         )
601: 
602:     # Validate the hierarchical segmentations
603:     validate_hier_intervals(reference_intervals_hier)
604:     validate_hier_intervals(estimated_intervals_hier)
605: 
606:     # Build the least common ancestor matrices
